plan.title: feat(authz): TOTP-armed operator delegation so the orchestrator can run terminal-only steps from a phone-only operator

narratives.Description: feat(authz): TOTP-armed operator delegation so the orchestrator can run terminal-only steps from a phone-only operator
narratives.Overview:
1. One core arming verb takes the prompt text and the host session id from a thin host adapter. It checks the TOTP code against the secret enrolled at a real terminal, accepts it only when its time step is greater than `lastAcceptedStep` in the protected delegation store, sets `lastAcceptedStep` to that step whenever a valid code is seen (even when the rest of the command is refused), and writes the record in the same locked step. A step at or below `lastAcceptedStep` is a quiet no-op.
2. The record holds the arm-time host session id, `expiresAt` (default 12h, max 72h) and the allowlist. The session id limits the record's life and labels the audit; it is not isolation between same-user agents, and the TTL is the real cap. `deft delegate off`, TTL, session end, UAT start, the kill switch and a terminal `deft authz:revoke` each end it.
3. While the record is live, #7279 harness-attended requests complete with a new provenance `delegated-totp` (not `host-user-event`), only for `scope:record-approved-scope` and `authz:grant` with one of the templates `release-cut`, `release-publish`, `release-rollback` or `release-promote-latest`. Every other harness-attended verb and template refuses. Completing a request is one compare-and-set from open to completed.
4. Grants and approved-scope stamps minted this way carry a distinct delegated origin, and exactly one consumer accepts each: the scope-provenance fence check (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts`) for a delegated approved-scope stamp, and `evaluateClosedVerb` (`packages/core/src/authz/closed-verb.ts`) for a delegated release grant, only for the release verb its template names. `isHumanOrigin`, `isHumanApprovalStamp`, the general grant check in `authz/evaluate.ts`, the #6138 `protected`-class floor and every other consumer keep refusing a delegated origin. A delegated grant or stamp expires no later than the delegation and stops admitting when the delegation ends.
5. Hook denies: the only delegable deny in this change is `prospective-scope-cover-deny`, and only for the advisory-capable scope-cover failure (targets resolved, staged paths read). It becomes allow-with-audit and the remaining checks still run. Unresolved targets, unreadable staged paths and index-changing forms still refuse. The inventory adds deny codes only in this per-condition form.
6. The install-health stop is removed rather than delegated: while the runtime is missing, the outer hook stub admits one standalone install invocation, the lockfile-matched command its refusal names, run with the stub's resolved project root as its working directory and with no extra arguments or chained commands. Every other tool call stays blocked.
7. Never delegable: the body's list, plus `finish-loop`, `gate-override` and `spec-drift-override` grants, grants with raw ops and no template, `authz:uat-*` and `authz:revoke`. The human merge gate is unchanged.
8. Each delegated mint or allow is audited with its provenance and posts one chat line. The docs state the strength as parity of forging effort with the terminal gate and a wider blast radius, name the passkey (#6945 / #7046) as the upgrade that makes the code unproducible by an agent, and say that under standing delegation the #7279 digest is not human review.

## Acceptance Criteria


- [ ] A valid code arms; a wrong or missing code, or a step at or below `lastAcceptedStep`, writes nothing; a valid code inside a refused command still advances `lastAcceptedStep`; a repeat of the same input is a quiet no-op.
- [ ] Two concurrent arms with the same code create one record, and two concurrent completions of one request complete it once.
- [ ] The record carries the arm-time session id and an expiry no later than 72h; a fixture shows that `delegate off`, TTL expiry, session end, UAT start, the kill switch and a terminal `authz:revoke` each end it.
- [ ] End to end for approved-scope: with a live record an agent shell mints a stamp, the scope-provenance fence check admits the stamped path, and after disarm the same stamp no longer admits; without a record the mint refuses as today.
- [ ] End to end for each of the four release templates: with a live record an agent shell mints the grant, `evaluateClosedVerb` admits the matching release verb and refuses every other verb, and after disarm the same grant no longer admits.
- [ ] A delegated grant or stamp is refused by `isHumanOrigin`, `isHumanApprovalStamp`, the general grant check, the #6138 `protected`-class floor and the other approved-scope readers.
- [ ] `prospective-scope-cover-deny` allows with audit only for the advisory-capable scope-cover failure and the remaining checks still run; unresolved targets, unreadable staged paths and index-changing forms still refuse.
- [ ] With the runtime missing, the hook stub admits its named install command run in the stub's project root, and refuses the same command in another working directory, with extra arguments, or chained with another command; every other tool call stays blocked.
- [ ] With a live record, `finish-loop`, `gate-override`, `spec-drift-override`, raw-ops grants, `authz:uat-*`, `authz:revoke` and the body's never-delegable list still refuse.
- [ ] Each delegated action is told apart from a terminal action by its provenance in the record and the audit, and posts one chat line.
- [ ] The docs state parity of forging effort, the wider blast radius, the passkey upgrade, and that the #7279 digest is not human review under standing delegation.
- [ ] Arming logic lives in one core verb; the Claude adapter passes only prompt text and session id; the Antigravity adapter follows #7332 and the two probes in amendment comment 7206768951.
- [ ] The inventory table is in the PR, with an outcome (delegable in the B5 form, remove, or human-only with a reason) for each stop.

**Verdict on the refutation target: refuted as worded, survivable as re-scoped.** The claim says the TOTP code is a factor a same-user agent "can neither produce nor replay". With symmetric TOTP, the verifier must hold the secret. The verifier is a hook process that runs as the operator's OS user, so the agent shell (same user) can read the same secret and compute any code. No storage choice under one OS user changes that. The second half ("at least as strong as today's terminal mint check") is closer to true **per act**: today's gate is also forgeable by a same-user process that drives a pseudo-terminal (the module names this the "pseudo-terminal residual"). But the proposal turns one forged act into a **standing** 12–72h authority over many mints and deny codes. Today a forge buys one mint. So the right claim is "equal effort to forge, wider blast radius". The design can bind if it says that and caps the blast radius (F2–F4). Only an asymmetric factor (passkey / signed approver, #6945 / #7046) makes the stronger claim true.

Verified at `f2e0e609` by pin-read. Line numbers are for this SHA.

### F1 — sharpens-framing — TOTP is "equal effort", not "unforgeable"; say so and name the flip

- **Evidence.** `packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts` `refuseNonInteractiveMint` / `admitHarnessAttendedMint`: under agent markers, a kept-mint verb completes with `isTty()` + `hasControllingTerminal()` + phrase `mint` read from `/dev/tty` or `\\.\CONIN$`. A process that owns a pty/ConPTY master owns that controlling terminal and can write `mint` into it (for example `script`, node-pty or ConPTY). `classify.ts` lists `script` only as a destination writer (lines ~338 / ~574), not as a mint forge. So today's gate stops cooperating agents and accidents, not a determined same-user process. TOTP with the secret on the same user's disk is the same class.
- **Failure mode.** The design text and later reviews rely on "the agent cannot produce the code". Later decisions then widen the allowlist on the basis of a property that does not exist (for example adding `gate-override`, see F2).
- **Disposition consequence.** Restate the target as "a deliberate forge costs about the same as forging today's terminal phrase; delegation widens what one forge buys". Record the flip condition: if Directive later must hold against a hostile same-user agent, only the asymmetric option (#6945 / #7046 passkey, verifier holds a public key only) is enough. Test point 2 resolves to: the operator's acceptance is sound for parity of effort, not for parity of blast radius.

### F2 — blocks-the-design — A delegated `authz:grant` mints a normal human-origin grant; the #6138 keep and `mintedVia` audit cannot hold as built

- **Evidence.** `packages/core/src/authz/actions.ts` `mintHumanOriginGrant` always calls `mintOperatorOrigin(...)`, and `store.ts` `mintOperatorOrigin` always sets `kind: "operator-cli"` and `actor` defaults to `"operator"`. `origin.ts` `isHumanOrigin` accepts any human kind with a non-agent actor. It never reads `mintedVia`. `closed-verb.ts` consumes grants only through `isHumanOriginGrant`. In `human-presence-mint.ts` the `completedVia` union is `"controlling-tty-phrase" | "host-user-event"`, and that value is stored only on the request file, not on the grant. `authz.ts` routes every `authz:grant` template (including `gate-override`, `spec-drift-override`, `release-publish`, `delivery-identity-attest`) through the same mint.
- **Failure mode.** With a live record, the agent asks for `authz:grant --template gate-override --target <refuseCode>`. The result is a grant indistinguishable from a terminal mint to every consumer: closed-verb admission, any #6138 `protected`-class floor that keys on human origin, and gate-integrity (#3156) overrides. The keep ("never the human-origin grant that opens `protected`") is violated through one hop. The `mintedVia: delegated:totp` AC becomes audit-only text, not a control.
- **Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind until it names both:
  1. a distinct origin for delegated mints (a new `GrantOrigin.kind`, or a `mintedVia` value that `isHumanOrigin` and the #6138 / closed-verb consumers **read and refuse** for the protected class), and a new `completedVia` / `provenance` value instead of reusing `host-user-event`;
  2. an explicit template allowlist. `gate-override` and `spec-drift-override` belong on the never-delegable list beside `policy:allow-*`: they are gate escapes, and the body's list omits them. Raw `--ops` grants without a template should stay human-only.

### F3 — sharpens-framing — Replay protection must be a monotonic time-step in the protected store, burned on any sighting

- **Evidence.** The body and amendment say "single-use", but do not say where the used state lives. The operator's code reaches the model context and the host transcript (Claude stores prompts in JSONL under the user profile, which the agent can read). RFC 6238 verifiers usually accept ±1 step (about 90 s).
- **Failure mode.** (a) If "used" is a set of codes in a file the agent can rewrite, deleting the entry re-opens the code. (b) If a prompt carries a valid code but fails another check (bad TTL, typo, wrong verb form) and the code is not burned, an agent that reads the transcript can replay it inside the window through a subagent hand-back. The probe shows hand-backs fire `UserPromptSubmit` with the parent `session_id`.
- **Disposition consequence.** State it in the lean. Store `lastAcceptedStep` in the protected delegation store. Accept only `step > lastAcceptedStep`. Advance it whenever a valid code is seen, even when the rest of the command is refused. This also covers the Antigravity "quiet no-op on repeat" AC deterministically: a repeat is `step <= lastAcceptedStep` → no write and no alarm, whatever the input text. Write-protection of that store is the existing shell classifier (`matchProtectedStoreShellDest`), which is heuristic. That is acceptable under F1's parity framing, but say so.

- **Evidence.** The body binds the record to the host session id. The mint process can learn its session only from env (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` / `CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SESSION_ID`), and any agent shell can set those. The probe shows child `claude` CLIs and agent-started sessions run the same hooks.

metadata.issueBody:
## Problem

Some Directive steps can only be done by a person at a local terminal:

- **Terminal mints.** `scope:record-approved-scope` and the `authz:*` mutators go through `refuseNonInteractiveMint` (`packages/runtime/src/human-presence-mint.ts`). It refuses agent shells, then needs a TTY, `--confirm`, and the word `mint` typed at the controlling terminal.
- **Hook denies with no grant escape.** The PreToolUse hook denies some agent tool calls. The only way past them is to run the step outside the agent. Examples:
  - the commit admission / `prospective-scope-cover-deny` (#6278) on chore and pin commits;
  - the install-health block ("Agent tool calls stay blocked until a person runs it").

When the operator is away from the computer and has only a phone (Remote Control), every one of these steps stops the work until they get back.

#7279 added a harness-attended request: a single-use request bound to a digest of the command, which a "host-authenticated user event" can complete. Nothing supplies that event yet (the default reader returns `null`).

## Probe evidence (Claude Code desktop, 2026-11-26)

A logging-only `UserPromptSubmit` hook showed:

- A message sent from a phone over Remote Control fires the hook, with the same `session_id` as desktop messages. Good.
- The hook **also** fires for prompts no person typed: a subagent hand-back delivered to its parent session, a prompt in an agent-started session (`dontAsk`, not attended), and a child agent CLI that runs the same Claude hook config. None of these carry an origin field.
- The agent shell exposes `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and `CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SESSION_ID`.

So the text of a prompt alone is **not** proof that the operator sent it. Arming needs a second factor that an agent cannot produce.

## Proposal: TOTP-armed standing delegation

1. **Arm from chat.** The operator sends `deft delegate on <ttl> <6-digit TOTP>`. A `UserPromptSubmit` hook checks the code against a TOTP secret enrolled once at a real terminal. On success, it writes a delegation record to a protected store (for example `.deft/authz/delegation/`), bound to the session id, with an expiry and an allowlist. Direct writes by an agent stay denied, as for every protected store.
2. **Terminal mints.** While the record is live, the record acts as the host-user-event, so the agent's harness-attended request is completed without the terminal phrase. Each mint stays single-use and bound to its command digest, and is stamped `mintedVia: delegated:totp`. Each delegated mint posts one line back to the chat.
3. **Hook denies.** The PreToolUse dispatcher reads the same record. While it is live, a short list of deny codes becomes "allow with audit".
4. **Disarm.** The operator sends `deft delegate off`. It also ends at TTL expiry (default 12h, max 72h), at session end, at UAT start, and on the kill switch. `deft authz:revoke` from a terminal also ends it.
5. **Never delegable:**
   - kill-switch on/off and kill-switch plants;
   - `authz:uat-*`;
   - `policy:allow-bot-merge`, `allow-direct-commits`, `allow-destructive-gh-verbs`;
   - `.deft/approvers.json`;
   - direct writes to the protected stores;
   - another session's live occupancy lease;
   - arming or extending the delegation itself.

   The human merge gate is unchanged.

## Inventory step

List every "a person runs it / from your own terminal" stop (runtime mints, hook denies, install-health, release-run steps) and give each one an outcome:

- **delegable** — added to the allowlist;
- **remove** — the stop is stale or not needed. For example, the release-run text still says to commit the pin "from your own terminal until #5771 lands", but #5771 is closed.
- **human-only** — with a reason.

Prefer **remove** where it is safe. The goal is fewer stops, not a new gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TOTP enrollment needs a real terminal (the current mint gate). The secret is stored outside the repo and is never printed after enrollment.
- [ ] `deft delegate on` with a valid code writes the record. A wrong or reused code, a missing code, or text from a non-attended or agent-delivered prompt writes nothing.
- [ ] With a live record, `scope:record-approved-scope` and the allowlisted `authz:grant` templates complete from an agent shell. Without one, they still refuse as today.
- [ ] The hook deny codes chosen in the inventory are allowed only while the record is live, and every allow is audited.
- [ ] Never-delegable verbs still refuse with a live record.
- [ ] `deft delegate off`, TTL expiry, session end, UAT start and the kill switch each end the record.
- [ ] Each delegated action can be told apart from a terminal action in the record (`mintedVia`) and in the audit.
- [ ] The inventory table is in the PR, with an outcome for each stop.

## Related

#7279 / #7272 (harness-attended mint), #6945 / #7046 (signed approvers; a passkey tap is a stronger later option for arming), #3801 (standing mandate: decision scope, not authentication), #6740 (kill switch), #6278 (commit admission), #4627 (no TTY needed).
